set_aside.subject: K-02 purity and sandbox trust boundary
set_aside.text: “no clock, no randomness” and “Agent-written code — untrusted forever” conflict with “guards against depending on the time or on chance by accident; it is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
set_aside.question: Is absence of clock and randomness an enforced invariant for adversarial agent-written code, or only a best-effort guard against accidental use?
options: Enforce the invariant even against deliberate circumvention
Only block ordinary uses and permit the purity claim to be violated by circumvention
Detect circumvention when possible and fail the execution, without guaranteeing detection
set_aside.default_guess: Treat no clock and no randomness as an invariant and refuse any detected attempt, while acknowledging that the specified mechanism is presently insufficient.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty corpus, and its submitted Python implementation obtains time through ctypes or another route around patched clock APIs.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel runs admission trials in the sandbox.
The implementation uses the obtained time to choose its declared output.
outcomes: An implementer treating purity as an invariant blocks the access and refuses admission for a sandbox violation.
An implementer treating the new wording as a best-effort accidental-use guard allows the trial and may admit the implementation.
witness.observer: The authoring agent sees refusal versus admission; later run callers can also see time-dependent outputs.

set_aside.subject: Clock and randomness API boundary
set_aside.text: “the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: Exactly which Python standard-library modules, functions, constructors and indirect facilities count as clock or randomness entry points that must be withheld?
options: Only direct APIs such as time and random
All standard-library APIs that expose time or entropy, including datetime, secrets, uuid and os.urandom
All direct and indirect routes, including generic facilities such as ctypes that can reach host clock or entropy sources
set_aside.default_guess: Block every documented standard-library API whose result depends on wall/monotonic time or system entropy, and treat generic escape facilities separately as sandbox violations.

witness.initial: A submitted implementation otherwise satisfies its contract and corpus.
events: The implementation calls datetime.datetime.now or os.urandom rather than time.time or random.
outcomes: An implementer with a narrow reading allows the call and returns successful trial evidence.
An implementer with a broad reading withholds the call and returns failed trial evidence.
witness.observer: The agent trying the implementation sees success versus failure.

set_aside.subject: Withheld clock or randomness access
set_aside.text: “The clock and randomness are withheld from a function that calls the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: What observable event occurs when a function calls a withheld entry point, and how is it classified in trials, real runs and traces?
options: The call is refused as a sandbox violation and the execution fails
The API is absent or raises an ordinary Python exception handled like any other function exception
The API returns a fixed deterministic substitute
The implementation is rejected before execution by code inspection
set_aside.default_guess: Fail the execution as a sandbox violation, recording the attempted facility without exposing host details.

witness.initial: An admitted or submitted implementation executes time.time during a trial or real run.
events: The kernel must produce trial evidence or a node trace and run status.
outcomes: One implementer reports a sandbox violation and fails the execution immediately.
Another exposes a missing/raising API as an ordinary Python exception, or supplies a fixed value, producing a different failure classification or even success.
witness.observer: The agent reading trial evidence or the owner/agent reading the run trace sees the difference.

set_aside.subject: K-05 deterministic admission after permitted circumvention
set_aside.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus” conflicts with “it is no guarantee against code written to get around it” when such code can obtain time or randomness during trials
set_aside.question: What preserves deterministic admission when an implementation deliberately reaches clock or randomness through an unblocked route?
options: Such access must always be detected and refuse admission
Admission determinism applies only after sandbox execution results have been produced, so identical submissions may receive different verdicts
Trial executions receive a reproducible virtual clock and entropy source even for indirect access
set_aside.default_guess: Require detected nondeterministic access to fail as a sandbox violation and define deterministic admission as the same verdict for the same implementation, contract and corpus.

witness.initial: A fixed implementation and fixed trial corpus are submitted twice; the implementation obtains entropy through a route not among the withheld entry points and passes only for one result.
events: The kernel performs the first whole-corpus admission.
The same content is submitted or evaluated again with the unchanged corpus.
The indirect entropy source yields a different value.
outcomes: Under the absolute deterministic-verdict passage, both evaluations must have the same verdict or the nondeterministic access must be refused.
Under the circumvention disclaimer, one evaluation can admit and the other refuse because the sandbox does not guarantee blocking the source.
witness.observer: The authoring agent and anyone inspecting admission records see inconsistent verdicts for unchanged inputs.
